restrictions: Exactly sha1-r79-prefix-v1: fixed standard IV, prefix rounds 0 through 78 on every padded block, standard FIPS 180-4 padding and feed-forward, full 160-bit digest, ordinary two-message collision only.

Two-block identical-prefix differential attack: messages P || B1 || B2 with a shared 64-byte prefix; block 1 maps chaining difference 0 to a fixed nonzero dO, block 2 maps dO back to 0 after round 78; the identical padding block preserves the collision.

Hard budgets: each near-collision block search is capped at 2^60.9 model units (one 79-round target compression = 1, any other 256-bit word operation = 1/1957); preprocessing charged at 2^50; verification at most 2^10; total at most 2^61.91 < 2^62 including all failed trials.

Analytic upper bound under explicitly declared heuristics H-path-79, H-search-exp, H-transfer, H-preproc with supporting experiment-backed H-local-add; no executed full-scale search, no stored collision, no certificate; the certificate manifest is intentionally empty.

The exact 79-round condition tables are not re-derived in this package; existence and cost of the paths rest on the published executed/benchmarked 80-round attacks, the published reduced-round lineage, and the stated one-round truncation argument. This disclosed gap is the exploratory-lane content of the claim.

The schema-required baseline_improved value sha1-r79-nominal-v2 is a reference identifier; the claimed scalar 62 is an honest numerical comparison against the nominal display exponent 80, which is not an established attack, qualified baseline, or security bound.

heuristics.statement: For the 79-round target there exist two differential near-collision paths in Wang's disturbance-vector family (block 1: chaining difference 0 to a fixed nonzero dO after round 78 with feed-forward; block 2: dO back to 0 after round 78 with feed-forward) whose standard message-modification/neutral-bit/boomerang search has expected per-block cost no larger than the published 80-round identical-prefix figures, i.e. expected total at most 2^61.2 compression-equivalents before the transfer adjustment of proof.md Section 8.
heuristics.scope: Complete fixed-IV 79-round SHA-1 (rounds 0..78), two-block identical-prefix ordinary collision; per-block search cost and path existence for the round-shifted disturbance vector.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the executed 80-round collision (2^63.1 spent, SHAttered), the benchmark-backed 80-round identical-prefix expectation 2^61.2 (Shambles), and the published reduced-round collisions at 64/70/73/75 steps (2^35, 2^44, 2^50.7, 2^57.7) from the same disturbance-vector family, to the unexecuted 79-round prefix target via one-round truncation.
heuristics.limitations: The exact 79-round condition tables are not exhibited or independently re-derived in this package; the claim relies on the structural truncation argument (fewer rounds carry no more conditions) plus the published round-scaling record. If no valid 79-round path with this cost exists, the claimed scalar fails.

heuristics.statement: Each near-collision block search behaves as a long sequence of low-probability trials whose cost to success is exponentially distributed with mean E_i, so a hard budget B_i succeeds with probability 1 - exp(-B_i/E_i); with B1 = B2 = 2^60.9 and E_1 + E_2 <= 2^61.4 the overall success probability is at least 0.507 for any split, claimed at 0.45.
heuristics.scope: Success-probability model of the two budgeted block searches under fresh independent algorithmic coins with the target fixed.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the observed agreement between pre-computed estimates and actually spent work in the executed 80-round attacks (SHAttered spent 2^63.1 against the 2^61 theoretical estimate; the Shambles chosen-prefix computation completed within its budgeted two months) to the tail behavior of the same search processes at 79 rounds.
heuristics.limitations: Per-trial independence is not proved and small-sample tail behavior is not directly observed at full scale; the claimed success probability 0.45 is set below the analyzed worst case 0.507 to absorb model error, and all failed trials are charged inside the budgets.

heuristics.statement: Published GPU SHA-1-equivalent totals for the 80-round attack transfer to collision-frontier-v5 model units for the 79-round attack at the ratio of one compression to its reference word-operation cost (1957 for sha1-r79 versus about 1982 for the 80-round figure), giving expected total at most 2^61.2 * (1982/1957) <= 2^61.22, used with margin as 2^61.4.
heuristics.scope: Conversion of the published measured work totals (which bundle round-function evaluations and all other word operations) into the organizer cost model.
heuristics.extrapolation: From GPU wall-clock-derived 80-round totals to the model's word-RAM prices; assumes the published implementations' non-compression word work is priced conservatively by the 1/1957 rate.
heuristics.limitations: Hardware-specific constants differ from the model's reference normalization; the ledger carries explicit margin and the executed SHAttered 2^63.1 anchors the upper side independently of the transfer.

heuristics.statement: One-time construction of the two 79-round differential paths (disturbance-vector selection and condition-table search with published tooling, starting from the public 80-round paths) plus the one-time prefix-block search costs at most 2^50 compression-equivalents, charged in total time.
heuristics.scope: Preprocessing only; excludes the online search, which is budgeted separately at 2^61.9.
heuristics.extrapolation: From published path-search practice (hashclash-style local search and joint local-collision analysis) to a conservative fixed bound; no precise historical figure is published.
heuristics.limitations: The 2^50 bound is an estimate; the claimed scalar is insensitive to it because even 2^58 preprocessing leaves the total below 2^62.

heuristics.statement: The local modular-addition XOR-differential transition probabilities used by the per-round path probability calculus of the cited attacks are exactly computable finite counts (for example: MSB flip of one addend gives an MSB-only output difference with probability 1; LSB flip of one addend gives an LSB-only output difference with probability 1/2).
heuristics.scope: Single modular additions at 8-bit width, exhaustively enumerated by the organizer evaluator; methodology evidence for the calculus underlying path probabilities.
heuristics.extrapolation: None claimed beyond the stated finite counts: the experiments do not establish any multi-round or full-scale probability, which remains covered by H-path-79.
heuristics.limitations: Exact 8-bit single-addition counts only; composed round behavior is not measured and is not claimed to follow from these checks.
